### Note.

It is necessary for the reader to study the *Book of the Three Principles* and the *Book of the Threefold Life of Man* along with this one; then he will be able to correctly understand the foundation <note>original: "Ground"; referring to the underlying spiritual basis or fundamental essence of his philosophy.</note> of this book, *Aurora* <note>Latin: "Dawn" or "Daybreak".</note>. For since the time of the writing of this book, *Aurora*—the "Day-spring" or "Morning Redness"—the lovely *Bright Day* has appeared to the author. Everything that is too obscure here is presented *most clearly* in those other books; this is truly a great wonder, as the reader who loves God will find.

Although the author had actually written this book only for himself, according to the gift of God’s Spirit, he did not know *then* God’s counsel or will concerning it.

# The Preface to the Reader.

## Reader,

The books of this *author* that are already published sufficiently demonstrate the high value of his deep writings. But among all the benefits that arise from them, one inestimable excellence is that they help the *minds* of all kinds of people (who will take the effort to read and consider them) in understanding the *Holy Scriptures*. They do so satisfactorily and convincingly, without needing to refer to the vast *commentaries* of *authors* written in either the *learned* <note>original: "Learned... Tongues"; referring to classical languages like Latin, Greek, and Hebrew.</note> or *modern tongues*. They will help *people* to discern the truth within the various *explanations* and *opinions* of all *factions*, and also help quiet the differences, debates, controversies, disputes, and contests. This allows everyone to be satisfied in a *loving and friendly* way, agreeing together in one and the same *truth*.

<margin>† Romans 8:3</margin>
<margin>† Romans 8:17</margin>

One group is judged for supposedly denying a *Christ without* <note>Referring to the historical, physical Jesus who lived and died on earth.</note>, and the other for denying a *Christ within* <note>Referring to the spiritual presence of Christ dwelling in the heart of the believer.</note>. Yet it should be considered that * *Christ is not divided*, though he is everywhere in all places and in all things, and was yet manifested only once in † the likeness of sinful *flesh*. He suffered, died, rose from the dead, and ascended into glory. But if we † *suffer with him*, we shall also be *glorified with him* at his appearing. *Paul’s* desire to

...glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power; sown in imperfection, it is raised in perfection. <margin>† 1 Corinthians 15:53, 54.</margin> For this mortal body must put on immortality. Thus, although we have risen with Christ in our souls, spirits, and minds—serving the law of God in this life with a perfect heart—and even though sin may dwell in our flesh, yet if we do not let it reign in our mortal or imperfect bodies (so that we do not obey its lusts), then the Holy Spirit lives in our minds and in our bodies, which are the temples of the Holy Ghost. But if we allow sin to reign, then our souls and bodies become dens of thieves and murderers, and the dwellings of all devils.

For the present, this is my understanding, which I pray may be enlightened and helped by the Father of Lights <note>James 1:17; a title for God as the source of all truth and goodness.</note>, from whom every perfect gift comes to myself and to all humanity, my brothers and sisters. They have various measures of the same light and different gifts from the same Spirit. I desire to share in these gifts with them and will rejoice greatly in doing so.

However, the foundation for understanding the things mentioned here, and everything contained in the Scriptures, is exactly described in this author’s <note>This likely refers to the mystic Jacob Boehme, whose works frequently use the terminology that follows.</note> writings.

For his writings reveal where the things themselves are to be found—in which all divine and natural mysteries are hidden. They also point out, as if with a finger, how those secret things have progressed into existence and manifestation from the infinite Incomprehensibility <note>original: "Incomprehensibility"; in this context, it refers to the "Unground" or the "Abyss," the divine state before any manifestation or creation.</note>, a state where nothing can be perceived, yet from which all things have come. They show how things have come to be as they are, leading us to discern what the Effable <note>term: Effable; that which can be expressed, spoken, or understood, as opposed to the "ineffable" or unspeakable nature of God's essence.</note> manifested, and revealed God is, as well as all other creatures. Finally, they reveal what we ourselves are and how we may attain the only true and eternal happiness and blessedness of everlasting life, with and in God.

*And can there be anything more useful, beneficial, necessary, and worthy than this?*

Also, further by his writings, we may come to understand how Christ is the Savior of **all** people—and yet not all will attain salvation. <header># Preface to the Reader.</header>

...concise terms very deeply expressed. But in this book, the foundations of those terms are described at length and clearly, in the manner of the infancy of his great revelation, in a simple way. Thus, it is a large and very clear primer <note>original: "A B C."</note>, being more suitable and plainer for beginners. Through it, his other books may be more easily understood. <margin>* Revelation 1:4, 3:1, 4:5, 5:6.</margin>
This is because it explains the first foundation concerning the Seven Properties of the *Eternal Nature*, which he calls here the *Seven Qualifying*—or fountain—Spirits or Qualities. These are * *the Seven Spirits of God, in, from, and for all eternity*. This edition includes *notes* of reference to the *Book of the Three Principles* and the *Threefold Life of Man*. These notes make up for the fact that this book was never finished. The author wrote these notes with his own hand as explanations in a manuscript belonging to *Michael von Endern*. His own original written copy had been taken from him by *Gregory Richter*, the *superintendent* <note>The ecclesiastical overseer or head pastor of the Lutheran church in the city of Görlitz.</note> at *Görlitz*. That original was published in print with many whole verses, lines, and words left out, printed in *German* <note>original: "high Dutch." In the 17th century, "Dutch" often referred to "Deutsch" (German).</note> in 1634. However, these *notes* were added by the author in the year 1620 and are inserted here with alphabetical marks in this translation into *English*. This translation is made from a copy taken from his own handwriting, which was kept hidden for twenty-seven years until November 26, 1641. At that time, it was brought to light by *D. P. S., a Burgomaster* <note>A city mayor or chief magistrate.</note> at *Görlitz*, and presented to the *Prince-Elector of Saxony’s* Marshal of the Household, *George Pflug*, in *Dresden*. It is now in the hands of a worthy person in *Holland* and was lately printed in *German*; the rest of the author’s manuscripts in his possession will also be printed.

<meta>This page begins the author's preface to the *Aurora*. It follows a list of corrections for the English translation, transitioning from editorial revisions to Jacob Boehme’s own introductory metaphors regarding the nature of knowledge and the cosmos.</meta>

<page-num>I</page-num>
<header>Jacob Boehme's Preface for the *Aurora*.</header>

## *To the Courteous Reader.*

->I.<-

Courteous reader, I compare the whole of philosophy, astrology, and theology—along with their mother—to a magnificent tree growing in a beautiful garden of pleasure.

2. Now, the earth in which the tree stands provides sap to the tree constantly, by which the tree possesses its living quality <term>In Boehme's writing, "quality" often refers to the German *Quall* or *Quelle*, meaning a fundamental force, source, or "fountain-spirit" that drives the nature of a thing.</term>. The tree itself grows from the sap of the earth, becoming large and spreading itself out with its branches. Just as the earth works its power upon the tree to make it grow and increase, the tree also works constantly with all the strength in its branches so that it might still bear good fruit in abundance.

3. But when the tree bears little fruit—and even those are small, shriveled, rotten, and worm-eaten—the fault does not lie in the will of the tree, as if it purposely desired to bear evil fruit, because it is a magnificent tree of good quality. Instead, the fault lies here: it is often subjected to great cold, great heat, mildew, caterpillars, and other worms. For the "qualities" in the deep <note>original: "the Deep." In Boehme's cosmology, this refers to the vast, spiritual, and physical expanse of the universe or the "Abyss" from which all things originate.</note>—influenced by the stars—spoil the tree, and that causes it to bear very little good fruit.

4. Now, the tree is of this condition: the larger and older it is, the sweeter the fruit it bears. In its younger years, it bears little fruit, which is crude and...

<sig>B</sig>
<meta>catchword: wild</meta>

<summary>In this opening of the preface, Jacob Boehme uses the allegory of a "Tree of Knowledge" to explain how philosophy, astrology, and theology are interconnected and influenced by cosmic forces. He argues that the quality of the "fruit" (knowledge or spiritual life) depends both on the tree's inner nature and the external influences of the stars and elements.</summary>

<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Aurora, allegory, Tree of Knowledge, Philosophy, Astrology, Theology, Quality, the Deep, cosmic influence</keywords>

--- Page 38 ---
<meta>This page continues Boehme's metaphorical preface, detailing the environmental factors that affect the "tree" (the world) and explaining what each part of the tree represents in his cosmological system.</meta>

<page-num>2</page-num>
<header>J. B. Preface for the Aurora.</header>

...caused by the wild nature of the ground or earth and the *excessive moisture in the tree*. Although it bears many beautiful blossoms, most of its apples fall off while they are still growing; this does not happen when it stands in very good soil or earth <note>original: "mould"</note>. Now, this tree also has a good, sweet quality, but there are *three* others which are contrary to it: namely, the bitter, the sour, and the astringent.

5. As the tree is, so will its fruit be, until the sun works upon them and makes them sweet, so that they take on a sweet taste; its fruit must also endure <note>original: "hold out"</note> rain, wind, and tempests.

6. But when the tree grows old, its branches wither and the sap rises *no more*; then, below the stem or trunk, many suckers grow. At last, twigs also grow from the root and make the old tree flourish, showing that *it* also was once a green twig and a young tree, and has now become old. For Nature, or the sap, struggles as long as it can until the trunk grows quite dry, and then it is to be cut down and burned in the fire.

7. Now observe what I have signified by this *comparison* <note>original: "similitude"</note>: the garden of this tree represents the *world*; the soil represents *nature*; the trunk of the tree represents the *stars*; by the *branches* are meant the *elements*; the fruit which grows on this tree represents *humanity*; the sap in the tree resembles the pure *Deity*. Now, humans were made out of nature, the *stars*, and the *elements*, but God the Creator reigns in all—just as the sap does in the whole tree.

8. But there are *two qualities in nature* which exist until the *judgment of God*: the *one* is pleasant, heavenly, and holy; the other is fierce, wrathful, hellish, and thirsty.

9. Now the good quality operates <note>original: "qualifieth"; a term Boehme uses to describe how the fundamental forces or "source-spirits" of nature act and interact</note> and works continually with all industry to bring forth good fruits, and the *Holy Ghost* reigns therein and affords it sap and life. The bad one springs and drives with all its effort to bring forth bad fruit continually, to which the devil affords sap and *hellish* flame. Now both are in the tree of Nature, and *Humans* <note>original: "Men"</note> are made out of that tree and live in this world, in this garden, *between both*, in great danger; suddenly the *Sun* shines on them; soon after, winds, rain, and snow fall on them.

10. That is, if a person elevates his spirit into the *Deity*, then the *Holy Ghost* moves, springs, and operates in him. But if he permits his spirit to sink into the world in lust toward *evil*, then the *Devil* and hellish sap stir and reign in him.

11. Just as the apple on the tree becomes corrupt, rotten, and worm-eaten when frost, heat, and mildew fall on it, and easily falls off and perishes; so does *Man* also when he allows the *Devil* to rule in him with his *poison*.

12. Now, as in *Nature* there exists, springs, and reigns both good and bad, even so it is in *Man*. But *Man* is the *Child of God*, whom He has made out of the best *kernel* <note>original: "Kernel of Nature"; the core essence or seed of being</note> of Nature, to reign in the good and to overcome the bad. Though evil sticks to him, just as in *Nature* the evil hangs on the good, yet he can overcome the evil if he elevates his spirit in God; for then the *Holy Ghost* stirs and moves in him and helps him to overcome.

13. As the good quality in *Nature* is potent to overcome the *evil*—for it is from God and comes from God, and the *Holy Ghost* is the *Ruler* therein—even so is the fierce, wrathful *quality* powerful to overcome in a *malicious*

He argues that while humans contain both qualities, they have the divine potential to overcome evil by elevating their spirits toward God.</summary>

14. But humanity has cast itself into fierce wrathfulness through the fall of *Adam* and *Eve*, so that evil hangs upon them; otherwise, their inner impulse and drive would be directed *only* toward the good. But now it is in *both*, and it is as St. *Paul* says: *Do you not know that to whomever you yield yourselves as servants in obedience, you are the servants of the one you obey, whether of sin leading to death, or of obedience to God leading to righteousness?* (Romans 6:16).

15. But because a person has an *impulse* or inclination toward both, they may lay hold of whichever they please; for they live in this world between *both*, and both *qualities*—the good and the bad—are within them. In whichever direction a person moves, they are endowed with that power, whether it be a holy or a hellish power. For *Christ* says, *My Father will give the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> to those who ask him* (Luke 11:13).

16. Besides, God commanded humanity to do good and forbade them from doing evil; even now He daily calls, preaches, and exhorts people toward the good. By this we see clearly enough that God does not will *evil*; rather, His will is *that His Kingdom should come, and His will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.* Now, because humanity is poisoned through sin, both the fierce, wrathful quality and the good quality reign within. Humans are now half-dead, and in their gross ignorance, they can no longer know God their Creator, nor Nature and its operation. Yet Nature has done its best effort from the beginning until now—to which God has given His Holy Spirit—so that it has at all times generated wise, holy, and *understanding* people. These individuals learned to know Nature and their Creator, and through their writings and teachings, they have always been a light to the world, through which

He notes that despite human ignorance caused by the Fall, God provides the Holy Spirit and wise teachers to illuminate the truth of Nature and the Creator.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Boehme's discussion of the dual forces within human nature, focusing on how the "wrathful" quality can overcome the "good" quality, leading to spiritual corruption and historical conflict between siblings and nations.</meta>

<page-num>5</page-num>
<header>J. B. Preface for the Aurora. 5</header>

God has raised his Church on Earth for his eternal praise. Against this, the Devil has *raged* and ruined many a noble branch <note>original: "Twigg," meaning a person or a lineage</note> through the wrathful fierceness in Nature, of which he is the *Prince* and God.

17. For Nature has many times prepared and equipped a learned, sensible man with good gifts, but then the Devil has done his utmost to seduce that man. He leads him into *carnal pleasures*, pride, a desire for wealth, and the pursuit of authority and power. In this way, the Devil has ruled over him, and the fierce, wrathful *Quality* <note>Boehme uses "Quality" to describe the fundamental forces or properties—such as wrath or love—that govern existence.</note> has overcome the good. His understanding, knowledge, and wisdom have been turned into *heresy* and *error*; he has mocked the Truth and become the author of great errors on earth, serving as a prominent leader of the Devil's army.

18. For the bad quality in Nature has wrestled, and still wrestles, with the good ever since the beginning. It has elevated itself and ruined many a noble fruit even in the mother's *womb*, as is plainly seen first in *Cain* and *Abel*, who came from the same womb. From his mother's womb, *Cain* was a despiser of God and proud; but *Abel*, on the contrary, was a humble man who feared God.

19. This same struggle is seen also in the *three sons of Noah*, as well as in *Abraham's* sons *Isaac* and *Ishmael* <note>original: "Ismael"</note>. It is especially evident in *Isaac's* sons, *Esau* and *Jacob*, who struggled and wrestled even in their mother's womb. Therefore God said, *Jacob I have loved, and Esau I have hated* (Genesis 25). This simply means that both qualities in Nature have vehemently wrestled with each other.

20. For at that time, when God moved in Nature and intended to *reveal* himself to the world through righteous *Abraham, Isaac,* and *Jacob*, and sought to raise a Church for himself on earth for his glory, then in Nature

The conflict over the root of the tree became so great that they forgot to eat the fruit of the sweet tree because of their controversy about its root.

51. By now, they cared for *neither* the Root nor the Tree. The Prince of Darkness had another plan, intending something else: when he saw that they would no longer eat from the good Tree but were only arguing about the Root, he perceived that they had grown very weak and faint, and that "wild nature" <note>Boehme's term for the unrefined, fallen, or wrathful state of existence</note> dominated them once again.

52. Therefore, he stirred them up to pride so that everyone supposed he had the Root right at hand. Each person insisted that others must look to him, listen to him, and revere him. Consequently, the common people <note>original: "Lay people"</note> were troubled and led into sin. They lived in carnal pleasures, following the desires of their wild nature, and served their own bellies in decadence. They placed their confidence in the fruit of the tree that moved over them all, believing that even though they fell into misery, *they might be healed by it.*

# The Contents of this Book, by way of Introduction.

->To this book, I have given this name, namely:<-

## The Root or Mother of Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology.

->And so that you may know what this book treats of,<-
->*Observe:*<-

# I.

1. In *Philosophy*, the **Divine power** is treated:

I. *What God is;*
II. *How, within the Being of God, Nature, the Stars, and the Elements are created.*
III. *From where everything has its origin <note>original: "Original"</note>.*
IIII. *How Heaven and Earth were created.*
V. *How Angels, Mankind, and Devils were created.*
VI. *How Heaven and Hell, and whatever is creaturely, were created, and what the Two Qualities <note>In Boehme's thought, the "Two Qualities" refer to the conflicting forces of light/love and darkness/wrath that exist within all of nature</note> are in Nature.*

All out of a true foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> in the knowledge of the Spirit, by the impulse and motion of God.

## II.

2. In *Astrology*, the following is treated:
I. *Of the powers of Nature, of the Stars, and of the Elements.*
II. *How all creatures proceeded from them.*
III. *How these forces impel and rule everything.*
IIII. *How they work in all things, and how good and evil are wrought by them in humans and beasts.*
V. *From where it comes that Good and Evil exist and reign in this world.*
VI. *Also how the Kingdom of Heaven and of Hell consist within these things.*

3. My purpose is not to describe the path, location, and name of every star, nor their annual conjunctions, oppositions, or squares <note>original: "Quadrat"; a square is an astrological aspect where celestial bodies are 90 degrees apart</note>, or things of that nature. I do not intend to describe what they influence yearly and hourly, which over a long period of time has been observed by wise, skillful, and expert men—those who were rich and vast in spirit through their diligent contemplation, observation, deep insight, calculation, and computation.

4. Neither have I studied or learned these technical methods, and I leave that to the scholars to discuss. My intention, instead, is to write according to the Spirit and inner sense, rather than through intellectual speculation.

## III.

5. In *Theology*, the following is handled:
I. *Of the Kingdom of Christ, and of what condition it is.*
II. *How it is set in opposition to the Kingdom of Hell.*

2. Yet if a person wishes to speak of God and say what GOD is, then:
I. One must carefully consider the powers in nature.
II. Also the whole of Creation, both Heaven and Earth.

<header>Of the Divine Being in Nature, and Chapter 1.</header>

# III. The Stars, the Elements, and the Creatures that have come from them. Also, the holy Angels, Devils, and Mankind; furthermore, Heaven and Hell.

## Concerning the Two Qualities in One.

->3.<-

In this investigation, we find *two qualities*—a *good* one and an *evil* one. These exist within one another as *one* thing in this world, within all powers, in the stars and the elements, and in all creatures. No creature in the flesh, living a natural life, can survive unless it possesses these two qualities.

## What a QUALITY Is.

<margin>
* Understanding what is here called a QUALITY is the foundation of all of *Jacob Boehme’s* <note>original: "Behme’s"</note> revelations and of all mysteries; his writings are merely descriptions of this concept. Throughout his work, the seven qualities are sometimes called the Seven Sources, Seven Species, Kinds, Manners, Circumstances, Conditions, Powers, Operations, or Faculties of a thing. They are also called the "Qualifying" or "Fountain Spirits," which provide, model, imagine, or frame the power, virtue, color, taste <note>original: "b Sound, Smell"</note>, figure, shape, constitution, substance, essence, and distinct being of all things. This applies to everything that ever was, is, shall be, or can be, throughout all eternity—within God and all creatures, in Heaven, in Hell, or in this world. They are also the forms or properties of Nature, which is the *Salitter* <note>A term coined by Boehme to describe the divine "sap" or the fundamental power of God acting as a sort of celestial matter.</note> or power of God. As such, they are the seven spirits of God, as mentioned in the Book of Revelation <note>original: "Revelations of John"</note>, Chapter 1:4, 3:1, 4:5, and 5:6.
</margin>

->4.<-

Now, one must consider what the word QUALITY means or represents.

A quality is the movement, boiling, springing forth, and driving force of a thing.

## Of Heat.

5. As, for example, *Heat* burns, *consumes*, and drives out everything that enters it which is not of the same property. On the other hand, it *enlightens* and warms all cold, wet, and dark things, and it compacts and hardens soft things.

## Of Light and Fierceness.

6. It also contains two other kinds within it, namely: 1. Light, and 2. Fierceness <note>original: "Fiercenesse"</note>. Take notice of them in this way: The light, or the heart of the heat, is in itself a pleasant, joyful gleam or luster, a power of *life*, an illumination and shine from something far away; it is a part or source of the heavenly Kingdom of Joy.

7. For it makes all things in this world *living* and moving; all flesh, trees, leaves, and grass grow in this world through the power of the light and have their life in it—namely, in the Good.

8. Conversely, it also contains a fierceness or wrath which burns, consumes, and destroys. This wrath or fierceness springs up, drives, and raises itself within the Light, and makes the light movable.

9. These struggle and fight together in their two-fold source <note>original: "fource"; here referring to the "fountain-spring" or origin of a power</note> as if they were one thing. It is indeed one thing, but it has a double source. *Light* exists in God without heat, but it does not exist that way in Nature.

10. For all qualities in nature are within one another as one *quality*, in the same way that God is all: and

11. Now, *Heat* reigns and predominates in all powers in Nature and warms them all, and it is *one* source or spring in all; for if it were not so, the water would be too cold, the earth would be congealed, and there would be no air <note>original: "Ayr"</note>.

12. Heat is *predominant* in everything—in trees, herbs, and grass—and it makes the water movable. Consequently, through the waters springing out of the earth, herbs and grass grow. It is therefore called a *quality* <note>original: "Quality"; here referring to an active, essential property or power</note> because it operates, moves, and boils in everything, and elevates everything.

13. But the *Light* within the heat gives power to all qualities, so that everything grows *pleasant* and joyful. Without light, heat does not benefit the other qualities but is a *perdition* <note>original: "perdition"; meaning ruin or destruction</note> to the good—an evil source or spring—for everything is spoiled in the fierceness or wrath of the heat. Thus, the light within the heat is a quickening <note>original: "quick"; meaning living or life-giving</note> spring or living fountain, into which the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> enters, but not into the fierceness or wrath.

14. Yet the heat makes the light movable so that it springs and drives forth, as is seen in winter; although the light of the sun is likewise upon the earth, the hot rays of the sun cannot reach into the earth, and that is the reason why no fruit grows.

## Of the qualification of the Cold Quality.

->15.<-

Cold is also a quality, just like heat. It "qualifies" <note>original: "qualifieth"; here meaning to act, manifest its power, or impart a specific property</note> or operates in all creatures that come forth in Nature, and in everything that moves within it: in humans, beasts, birds, fish, worms, leaves, and grass.

16. Heat is set in opposition to it and operates within it as if they were one and the same thing; however, cold opposes the fierceness or rage of the heat and tempers <note>original: "allayeth"</note> it.

17. It also contains two sorts or species <note>original: "Species"; meaning types, varieties, or outward appearances</note> within it, which should be noted: namely, it mitigates the heat and makes all things pleasant. It is a quality of life in all creatures, for no creature can survive without cold, because it is a springing, driving mobility in everything.

18. The other kind or species is "fierceness." For where it gains power, it suppresses and spoils everything, just as heat does. No life can survive in it if heat did not prevent that. The fierceness of cold is the destruction of every life and the house of death, just as the fierceness of heat also is.

Heat and Cold work powerfully and fill everything, which causes a lively and *stirring* motion. But when cold *tempers* <note>original: "allayeth"</note> or *mitigates* the heat, then both their qualities are rarified and made thin; and the *bitter* quality <note>In the author's system, the "bitter" quality is one of the primary forces that creates tension and movement.</note> draws them together so that they become dewy.

20. But the air <note>original: "Ayr"</note> has its origin <note>original: "original"</note> and greatest motion from *heat*, and the water has its origin from *cold*.

21. Now these two qualities wrestle continually with one another; the heat *consumes* the water, and the cold condenses or crowds the air. Air is a cause and the spirit of every life and motion in the world, whether it is in flesh or in any of the plants <note>original: "vegetables"</note>. Everything that exists has its life from the air, and nothing that moves and exists in this world can survive without air.

24. Now in these two qualities, two other species <note>original: "Species"; here meaning types or manifestations</note> or kinds are to be observed: namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, a *living* and a *dead* operation. The air is a living quality if it is temperate or moderate in a thing, and the Holy Ghost reigns in the calmness or meekness of the air, and all creatures rejoice in it.

25. But there is also a *fierceness* <note>original: "fiercenesse"; often used to describe the "wrathful" or destructive side of nature in this period's mystical philosophy</note> or wrath in it, so that it kills and destroys by its terrible disturbance. Yet the interaction <note>original: "qualification"</note> takes its origin from this fierce disturbance or elevation, so that it moves and drives within every creature, and from this, *life* has its origins.

# The Bitter Quality

->28.<-

The *bitter* quality <note>In Jakob Böhme’s mystical philosophy, the "bitter quality" is one of the fundamental forces of nature, representing tension, attraction, and the "sting" that creates movement and individual form.</note> is the heart in every life; for just as it draws together the water in the *air* and also scatters <note>original: "dissipateth"</note> it so that it becomes separable, so it does in other creatures, such as the plants <note>original: "vegetables"</note> of the earth. Leaves and grass get their *green* color from the *bitter* quality.

29. Now, if the *bitter* quality dwells meekly and gently in any creature, then it is the *heart* or *joy* within it; for it dispels all other evil influences and is the beginning or cause of joy and *laughter*.

30. For when it is moved, it causes the creature to tremble and be joyful, raising it up in its whole body. It is, as it were, a glimpse or ray of heavenly joy—an elevation of the spirit, a spirit and power or virtue <note>original: "vertue"</note> in all the plants of the earth, and a mother of life.

## Of the Sweet Quality.

->34.<-

The *sweet quality* is set opposite to the *bitter*, and is a *gracious, amiable*, blessed, and pleasant quality. It is a refreshing of life and a soothing of the fierceness; it makes everything pleasant and *friendly* in every creature. It makes the *plants* <note>original: "vegetables"</note> of the earth fragrant and of good taste, producing beautiful yellow, white, and ruddy colors.

35. It is a glimpse and source of meekness, a pleasant habitation of heavenly joyfulness, a house or mansion of the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>, a quality of love and *mercy*, and a joy of life.

36. But on the other hand, it also has a fierce or wrathful source—a source of death and corruption. For if it is kindled within the *bitter quality* in the element of *water*, then it breeds diseases and the "botchy" <note>The "botchy" plague refers to the bubonic plague, characterized by "botches" or swollen sores.</note> *plague or pestilence* and the corruption of the flesh.

37. But if it is kindled in heat and bitterness, then it infects the element of *air*, by which is produced <note>original: "ingendred"</note> a sudden, spreading *plague* and sudden *death*.

# Of the Sour Quality.

->38.<-

The *Sour Quality* is set opposite to the bitter and sweet, and it is a good tempering agent <note>original: "temper"</note> for all things. It provides refreshing and cooling when the bitter and sweet qualities are heightened <note>original: "elevated"</note> too much. It is a longing delight in taste, a pleasure of life, and a stirring, boiling, flowing joy in everything. It is a desire, longing, and yearning for joyfulness—a quiet joy or dwelling place <note>original: "habitation"</note> of the *Spirit*. Thus, it serves as a balance <note>original: "temperature"</note> for all living and moving creatures.

39. It also contains a source of evil and decay <note>original: "corruption"</note>. For if it is heightened too much, or stirs too much *in anything so that it becomes inflamed*, then it produces *sadness and melancholy* <note>In the 1600s, melancholy was considered a physical ailment caused by an imbalance of "black bile," leading to deep depression.</note>.

40. In water, it causes a stink, rottenness <note>original: "putridnesse"</note>, and rankness; a forgetfulness of all good things, a melancholy or sadness of life, a House of Death, a *beginning of sorrow*, and an *end of joy*.

# Chapter 2. Further Concerning the Two Qualities.

->Now observe here further:<-

### 46.
*The whole body, up to the neck,* signifies and is the round circle or sphere of the stars, as well as the deep space within or between the stars, where the *planets* and *elements* rule.

### 47.
The *flesh* signifies the earth, which is solidified <note>original: "congealed"</note> and has no motion of its own. Therefore, the flesh in itself has no reason, understanding <note>original: "comprehensibility"</note>, or movement, but is moved only by the power of the *stars*, which rule in the flesh and veins.

### 48.
The earth could no more bring forth any fruit, nor could any metals like gold, silver, copper, iron, or stones grow within it, if the *stars* did not work within them. Neither could any grass grow without the operation of the *stars*.

### 49.
The head signifies *heaven*. It is attached to the body by the veins, passages, and the outflow of powers; thus, all the powers return from the head and *brain* into the body, into the "fountain-veins" or arteries of the flesh.

### 50.
Now heaven is a pleasant palace of joy, containing all the powers found in the rest of nature—the stars and elements—but they are not as harsh or forceful in their operation <note>original: "hard working and springing"</note>. For every power of *heaven* has only one type <note>original: "species"</note>, kind, or form of power, which arises very brightly and gently <note>original: "meek"</note>. These powers are not mixed with both evil and good as they are in the stars and elements, but are very pure.

### 51.
It is made from the midst of the *waters*, but does not function <note>original: "qualifying"</note> in the same way as the water in the elements, for there is no fierceness or wrath in it. However, heaven belongs to Nature because the stars and elements have their origin and power from *heaven*.

# Further Concerning the Two Qualities. Chapter 2.

52. For heaven is the *heart* of the water; just as in all creatures and in everything within this world, water is the *heart* of it. Nothing can exist <note>original: "Subsist"</note> without water, whether it is in the flesh or out of the flesh, in the plants <note>original: "Vegetables"</note> of the earth, or in metals and stones. In everything, water is the kernel or the *heart* of it.

53. And so heaven is the *heart* in nature, containing all the powers just as they exist in the stars and elements. It is a soft, flexible, and gentle <note>original: "meek"</note> substance of all powers, just as the *brain* is in a person's *head*.

54. Now heaven ignites the stars and elements with its power so that they move and work. In the same way, the *head* of a person is also like heaven.

55. For as all powers in heaven are gentle and full of joy, and as heaven has a *boundary* <note>original: "Closure"</note> or *firmament* above the *stars*—and yet all powers go out from heaven into the stars—so the *brain* also has a *boundary* or *firmament* between it and the body. Nevertheless, all the powers flow out from the *brain* into the body and into the entire person.

56. The head contains the *five senses*—namely: seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and feeling—in which the stars and elements interact <note>original: "qualify"</note>. Within these exists the sidereal <note>original: "Sydereal"; relating to the stars</note>—or heavenly, starry, or astral—and natural spirit in humans and animals. From this flow both good and evil, for the head is the *house* of the stars.

57. The stars borrow such power from heaven that they can create a living and moving spirit within the flesh of humans and animals. The movement of heaven makes the stars move, and so the head also makes the body move.

*Now open the eyes of your spirit here, and behold God your Creator.*

# Chapter 2. Further Concerning the Two Qualities.

->Question.<-

Now the question is this: From where does Heaven get—or from where does it borrow—this power that causes such *mobility* <note>original: "Mobility"; movement or activity</note> in *nature*?

->Answer.<-

59. Here you must lift up your eyes beyond nature, into the holy light of the triumphant divine power—into the unchangeable holy Trinity. This is a triumphant, springing, and moving Being, and all powers exist within it, just as they do in nature.

60. For this is the *Eternal Mother of Nature*, from which heaven, earth, stars, elements, angels, devils, humans, beasts, and all things have their being; and within this Mother, everything exists.

61. When we name heaven and earth, stars and elements, and all that is within them—and everything that is above the heavens—we are naming the *Total God* <note>original: "Totall God"; God in His entirety or the wholeness of the divine manifestation</note>. He has expressed himself in a *creaturely* <note>original: "Creaturely"; in the form of created beings or physical existence</note> way in these aforementioned beings, through the power that goes forth from Him.

62. But God in His Trinity is unchangeable. Whatever exists in heaven, on earth, or above the earth has its spring-source and origin from the *power* that proceeds from God.

63. Yet you must *not* therefore imagine that there is both good and evil within God. For God Himself is *Good*, and He takes His *name* from *goodness*, which is triumphant eternal joy. It is only that all the powers you can find in nature—and which exist in *all things*—proceed from Him.

->Question.<-

64. Now perhaps you may say: *Is there not good...* <note>The text continues on the next page with the catchword "and".</note>

65. For the bile makes the *astral spirits* <note>original: "Astral spirits"; the celestial or "star-derived" forces within the human body that govern life, movement, and temperament</note> active, joyful, triumphant, or laughing; it is the source of joy.

66. But if it is inflamed or ignited in one of the elements, it ruins the whole person; for the wrath in the astral spirits comes from the bile.

67. That is, when the bile overflows and runs to the heart, it ignites the element of *fire*. That fire then ignites the astral *spirits* which *rule* in the *blood* in the veins and in the element of *water*. Then the whole body trembles because of the wrath and the poison of the bile.

68. *Joy* has the same source and originates from the same substance as *wrath*. That is, when the bile is ignited within the *loving* or *sweet* quality regarding something a person is in love with, then the whole body trembles for joy. In those moments, the *astral* spirits are often affected when the bile overflows and is ignited within that *sweet* quality.

69. *But it does not have this same physical nature in God, for He does not have flesh and blood. Instead, He is a Spirit in whom all powers exist, as we pray in the Lord’s Prayer: "Yours is the power" (John 4:24, Matthew 6).*

70. And as it is written of Him in *Isaiah 9: "He is Wonderful, Counselor, Power, Hero <note>original: "Champion"</note>, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace."*

71. The bitter quality is also in God, but not in the same way as bile is in a human. Rather, it is an *ever-*

### The Third Chapter.

->**Concerning the most blessed, triumphant, Holy Holy Holy Trinity: GOD the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, the one and only God.**<-

->1.<-

Kind reader, I would have you faithfully advised here to let go of your preconceived opinions and ego. Do not seek out **pagan** <note>original: "Heathenish"; referring to classical philosophy or secular logic that relies on human intellect rather than spiritual insight</note> wisdom, nor be offended by the simplicity of the author. # The Fourth Chapter.
### Of the Creation of the Holy Angels.

->*An Instruction, or Open Gate of Heaven.*<-

->1.<-

The learned, and almost all writers, have very much encumbered <note>original: "cumbred"</note> and troubled their heads mightily to search, devise, and conceive in Nature—and have brought forth many and various opinions—concerning how and from what the holy angels were formed. And on the other side, what that horrible *fall* of the great prince *Lucifer* was; or how he became such a base, wicked, and fiercely wrathful devil; from where that *evil quality* should spring, or what drove him to it?

2. And although this fundamental <note>original: "ground"</note> and great mystery has remained hidden from the beginning of the world, and human flesh and blood is not able to conceive or apprehend it:

3. Yet **God**, who created the world, will reveal himself now, at the end of time, and all great mysteries will be manifested or revealed. This is to indicate that the great Day of Revelation and the Final Judgment is near and to be expected daily.

<summary>The author introduces a discussion on the creation of angels and the fall of Lucifer, noting that while these mysteries have long puzzled scholars and stayed hidden from humanity, God is now revealing them as the Final Judgment approaches.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Holy Angels, Lucifer, The Fall, evil quality, divine revelation, Final Judgment, Jacob Boehme</keywords>

--- Page 115 ---
<meta>This page continues from page 74, concluding the introductory remarks on the end times and beginning a detailed explanation of the divine nature and the creation of angels.</meta>

4. At that time, everything that was lost through *Adam* will be restored; and during this period, the Kingdom of Heaven and the kingdom of the devil shall be separated from one another, even in this world.

5. But *how* all this will be done, God will reveal with the greatest clarity and simplicity, so that no one will be able to oppose him.

6. Therefore, everyone should lift up their eyes, for their redemption draws near. Do not *seek* after base greed, pride, and indulgent, luxurious status, as if this were the best life to be found here; for in their luxury, such people sit in the middle of hell, serving as *the personal guard* for Lucifer.

7. They will soon certainly see this for themselves with great terror, anguish, and eternal despair, as well as to their own shame and disgrace. The devils are a terrible example of this; they were once the fairest and brightest angels in heaven, as I shall reveal, write, and demonstrate in the following pages. I will yield to God’s impulse, for I am not able to resist it.

# The Fifth Chapter.

## *Of the Corporeal Substance, Being, and Property of an Angel.*

-> *Question.* <-

1. Now the question here is: what kind of *body*, form, or shape does an angel have, or what is its figure?

-> *Answer.* <-

2. Just as man is created in the image and likeness <note>original: "similitude"</note> of God, so too are the angels. For they are the *brothers of men*, and *in the resurrection, people will have* no other form or image than the *angels* have, as our King CHRIST himself testifies in Matthew 22:30.

3. Besides, the angels *never* showed themselves in any other form or shape to people here on Earth than in a human form and shape.

4. Therefore, seeing as in the resurrection we shall be like the angels, the angels must necessarily be shaped and formed like us. Otherwise, we would have to take on *another* image or shape in the resurrection, which would be against and contrary to the original creation.

5. Thus also *Moses* and *Elijah* <note>original: "Elias"</note> appeared to the disciples of *Christ* in their own form and shape *on Mount Tabor*, though they had been in heaven for a long time before (Matthew 17).

6. And *Elijah* was taken up into heaven alive with his *living body*, and yet he had *no* other form or shape than he had when he was on earth (2 Kings 2:11).

7. Also, when *Christ* went to heaven, two *angels* hovered in the clouds and said to the disciples: "*Men of Israel, what are you looking for? This JESUS shall come again, just as you have seen HIM go away into heaven*" (Acts 1:11).

8. ## Of the *Qualification* of an Angel

### Question

35. The question now is: what kind of qualification <note>original: "qualification"; in this context, the author refers to the way internal properties or "qualities" interact and operate within a being</note> does an angel have?

### Answer

36. The *holy soul* of a man and the *spirit* of an angel share one and the same substance and being. there is no difference between them except in the *quality* itself, or their corporeal government. That which qualifies *outwardly* (or from the outside) in man—through the air—has a corrupt, earthly quality; yet, on the other hand, it also has a *divine* and *heavenly* quality that is hidden from [other] creatures.

37. But the *holy soul* understands it well, as the kingly prophet *David* says: *The Lord rides on the wings of the wind* (Psalm 104:3).

### Question

38. But a simple person may ask: what do you mean by the word *qualifying*, or what is that?

### Answer

39. I mean by that the power which *enters* into the body of the angel from the outside and comes out again. To use a comparison <note>original: "Similitude"</note>: it is like when a person draws a breath and breathes it out again; for in that process lies the life of both the body and the spirit.

# The Sixth Chapter.

## How an Angel, and a Human, is the Likeness and Image of God.

1. Behold! Just as the *essence of God* <note>original: "Being in God"</note> is, so is the essence also in *humanity* and *angels*. As the *Divine Body* is, so also is the *angelic* and *human body*, or *physicality* <note>original: "Corporeity"</note>.

2. But there is only this difference: an *angel* and a *human* are *created beings* <note>original: "Creature"</note>, and *not the whole of Being*. Rather, they are a *Son* of the whole Being, whom the whole Being has generated. Therefore, it is appropriate that they should be in *subjection* to the whole Being, since they are the *Son of its Body*.

3. Now, if the *Son* resists and opposes the *Father*, it is only right that the *Father* should cast him out of the *House*. This is because the *Son* sets himself against the one who generated him, and from whose power he became a *created being*.

4. For if anyone makes something out of what belongs to him, and if it does *not* turn out according to his will, he may do with it what he pleases—*making it either a vessel of honor or dishonor* <note>A biblical allusion to the potter and the clay in Romans 9:21</note>. This is exactly what happened to *Lucifer*.

->Now Observe:<-

5. From all its *qualities*, the *whole Divine power* of the Father speaks forth the WORD—that is, the Son of God.

<summary>This chapter explains that humans and angels are physical and spiritual reflections of God's own essence, though as created beings ("Sons"), they are rightfully subject to God's authority.</summary>

# Chapter 6: How an Angel and a Human are the Image of God.

6. Now that Voice, or *that* WORD, which the Father speaks, goes forth from the Father’s *Salitter* <note>original: "Salitter"; Boehme’s term for the divine powers or the "salt" of the spiritual earth</note> or powers, and from the Father’s *Mercurius* <note>original: "Mercurius"; referring here to the active, vibrating quality of sound, movement, or life</note> Sound or Tune. And the Father speaks this forth within himself, and *that* WORD is the very splendor or brilliance proceeding from all his powers.

7. But when it is spoken forth, it stays or remains *no longer* within the powers of the Father alone, but echoes or resonates back throughout the whole Father, *in all his powers*.

8. Now that WORD, which the Father *pronounces* or speaks forth, has such *sharpness* that the tone of the WORD goes swiftly, in a moment, through the entire depth of the Father; and that *sharpness* is the *Holy Spirit*.

<margin>* or Proclamation.</margin>

9. For the WORD, which is spoken or uttered, remains as a splendor or glorious *edict* <note>original: "Edict"; a formal decree</note> before the King;

10. But the tone or sound, which goes forth through the word, carries out the edict of the Father—which he had spoken through the Word—and that is the *birth* or generation <note>original: "Geniture"</note> *of the Holy Trinity*.

11. Now behold! An angel and a human are also like this: the power in the entire body has all the *qualities*, just as they exist in God the Father.

12. And just as all the powers in God the Father rise up from eternity to eternity, so all the powers also rise up in an angel and in a human, up into the *head*. They cannot rise any higher than that, for they are only created beings <note>original: "Creatures"</note> who have a beginning and an end.

13. And in the head is the *divine* council-seat or throne, and it represents God the Father; and the *five senses* or qualities are the counselors, who

14. Now the *five senses* always sit in council within the power of the whole body, and when the council's decree is concluded, then the solidified or combined *Judge* <note>The "Judge" here refers to the unified faculty of the mind or will that decides based on sensory input.</note> speaks it out into the center or midst of the body as a *WORD* into the heart; for that is the fountain of all powers, from which it also takes its rise.

15. Now it stands there in the heart as a *self-subsisting person*, composed of all powers, and is a Word; it signifies God the *Son*. And now it goes out from the *heart* into the *mouth* and onto the *tongue*, which is the *sharpness*; and the tongue so sharpens it that it sounds forth and is *distinguished* according to the *five senses*.

16. From whatever quality the word takes its origin, in that quality it is thrust forth upon the tongue; and the power of the *distinction* or *difference* goes forth from the *tongue*, and that signifies the *Holy Spirit* <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>.

17. For just as the *Holy Spirit* goes forth from the *Father* and the *Son*, and *distinguishes* and *sharpens* all things, and effects or produces that which the *Father* speaks through the *Word*;

18. So also the *tongue* sharpens, articulates, and distinguishes all that which the *five senses* in the head bring through the heart onto the *tongue*. And the *spirit* goes forth from the *tongue* through the *Mercurius* <note>original: "Mercurius"; referring to the active, vibrating principle of sound, motion, and communication</note> or tone in that place, as it was decreed or concluded by the *council of the five senses*, and executes it all.

## Of the Mouth.

->19.<-

The *Mouth* signifies that you are an un-almighty son of your Father, whether you are an angel or a human. For through the mouth you must draw the power of your Father into yourself if you wish to live.

20. An angel must do so as well as a human, though indeed he does not need to use the element of *air* in the same way as a human does; yet he must attract into himself, through the mouth, *the Spirit from which the air in this world exists.*

21. For in heaven there is *no* such air, but the qualities are very mild and joyful, like a pleasant, cheering breath of wind; and the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> is among all the qualities in the *Salitter* <term>Salitter: the divine "earth" or essential substance of heaven, often compared to saltpeter in alchemical thought</term> and *Mercurius* <term>Mercurius: the active, vital power or "Mercury" that drives motion, communication, and life</term>.

22. And the angel must also make use of this, or else he cannot be a *movable* creature, for he must also eat of the heavenly fruit through the mouth.

23. You must *not* understand this in an *earthly* way, for an angel has no guts, neither flesh nor bones, but is constituted or composed by *divine* power in the shape, *form*, and manner of a human. He has all members like a human, except for the organs of reproduction and the anus <note>original: "fundament"</note> or the exit for the *waste* <term>original: "draffe"; meaning dross, refuse, or physical excrement</term>; an angel has no need of them.

24. For man got his organs of reproduction and anus only in his doleful and lamentable fall. An angel sends forth nothing but the *divine* power—

25. But the heavenly fruits which he eats are *not earthly*. Though they are in such a form and shape as earthly ones are, yet they are pure *divine* power. They have such a pleasant, lovely taste and smell that I cannot liken it to anything in this world, for they *taste* and *smell* of the *Holy Trinity*.

26. You must not think that they are there only as a type <note>original: "Type"; here meaning a symbolic representation or shadow</note> or shadow of things. *No*: for the Spirit shows plainly that in the heavenly splendor—in the heavenly *Salitter* <term>Salitter: the divine substance or "earth" of the celestial realm</term> and *Mercurius* <term>Mercurius: the active, vital power that drives life and motion</term>—there grow *divine* trees, plants, and flowers of all sorts. Whatever exists in this world is but a type and resemblance of them. And just as the angels are, so are the vegetation and fruits; they are all *from* the divine power.

27. You must not equate these heavenly sprouts and growths entirely to those of this world. For there are two *qualities* <term>qualities: the inherent forces or properties of nature, which the author believes are in conflict on earth but unified in heaven</term> in this world: a *good* one and an *evil* one. Many things grow through the power of the evil quality, which is *not the case* in heaven.

28. For heaven has but *one* form or manner; nothing grows there which is *not good*. Only Lord Lucifer has deformed and fashioned <note>original: "dress'd"</note> this world in that manner. And therefore Mother *Eve was ashamed when she had* eaten of that which was fashioned by the *evil* quality; in the same way, she was also ashamed of her reproductive organs <note>original: "members of Generation"</note>, which she had caused <note>The author implies that the physical nature of these organs changed or became a source of shame specifically because of the Fall</note> by biting of this apple.

### Chapter 6. How an Angel and a Human are the Image of God.

...such a substance. Indeed, it is most certain and true that *there are all manner of* fruits in *heaven*, and *not* merely types <note>original: "Types"; here meaning symbolic representations or shadows</note> and shadows. Also, the angels pluck them with their hands and eat them, just as *we do* who are human; but they do *not* need any teeth to do so, *nor do they have any*, for the fruit is made of divine power.

30. Now all of this—whatever an angel makes use of that is external to <note>original: "without"</note> them for the support of their life—is *not* their own corporeal property <note>original: "propriety"; meaning legal ownership or an inherent part of their nature</note>, as if they held it by a natural right. Rather, the *heavenly* Father gives it to them in love.

31. It is true that their body is their own property, for God has given it to them as a possession. Now, whatever is given to anyone as their *own* property belongs to them by *right of nature*; it is not a righteous act to take it from them again, unless by some prior condition or agreement. God does *not* do this either; therefore, an angel is an eternal, incorruptible creature who stands or subsists throughout all eternity.

32. But how would the body *benefit* them if God did *not* feed it? For then it would have no mobility and would lie still like a dead block. Therefore, the angels are obedient to God and humble themselves before the powerful God. They honor, laud, and praise him in his great deeds and works of *wonder*, and sing continually of God’s *holiness*, *because* he feeds them.

# How an Angel and a Human are the Image of God. Chapter 6.

### Regarding the Gracious, Blessed, and Joyful Love of the Angels toward God, from a True Foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>.

->33.<-

True *love* in the *divine* nature comes from the *fountain* of the Son of God. Look here, child of man, let this be told to you: the angels *already* know what true love toward God is, but you need it in your *cold heart*.

34. Observe: when the gracious, kind <note>original: "amiable"</note>, blessed, joyful glance and light, together with the *sweet* power from the Son of God, shines into all powers within the whole Father; then *all* the powers are kindled by the gracious, kind, blessed, lovely *light* and sweet power in a triumphant and joyful manner.

35. In the same way, when the gracious, kind, blessed, and joyful light of the Son of God *shines* on the loving angels and casts its beams into their hearts, then all the powers in *their* bodies are kindled. And there arises such a *joyful* love-fire that, out of great joy, they sing and ring out praises—something that neither I nor any other creature is able to express.

36. I would have the reader *summoned* <note>original: "cited"</note> with this song into the next life, where they will experience it themselves; I am not able to set it down in writing.

37. But if you want to experience it in *this* world, *give up* your hypocrisy, bribery, deceit, and your mocking, and turn your heart in all serious-

# The Seventh Chapter.

->*Concerning the Court, Residence, and Dwelling, as well as the Government of Angels: How it stood in the beginning, after the Creation, and how it has become as it is now.*<-

->I.<-

At this point, the Devil will oppose like a snarling dog <note>original: "Snarling Dogg"</note>, for his shame will be exposed. He will give the reader many a forestroke <note>term: an initial blow or preemptive strike, as in sword fighting</note> and will always make the reader doubt that these things are true.

2. For nothing torments him more than when his former glory is thrown in his face <note>original: "upbraided to him"</note> by pointing out what a glorious king and prince he once was. When this is raised against him, he falls into a rage and madness, as if he would storm and overthrow the whole world.

3. If this chapter should be stumbled upon by a reader in whom the fire of the Holy Spirit is somewhat weak, I fear the Devil would be very busy attacking them, tempting them to doubt whether the things set down here are true or not. He does this so that his kingdom might not appear so naked and his shame might not be so completely exposed.

4. Now, if he even suspects he can succeed in causing doubt in any heart, he will not fail to use his utmost skill, effort, and labor to do so. I can see very clearly already that this is his intention.

5. Therefore, I want the reader to be warned: be diligent and patient in reading this.

->Question.<-

20. Now one may ask: what kind of substance or thing is it, that the Son of God is generated in the center or *midst* of these three kingdoms? Surely one angelic host must be nearer to him than the others, since their kingdom has such a great *depth*?

21. Also, would the glory, clarity, or *brightness* and power of the Son of God not be as great *outside* or *beyond* those kingdoms as it is *among* those who are near him, within the angelic circle or court?

->Answer.<-

22. *Answer:* The holy angels were made to be creatures from God, so that they should praise, *sing, ring* forth, and *shout for joy* <note>original: "jubilate"</note> before the Heart of God (who is the Son of God) and *increase* the heavenly joy.

23. *Where* else would the Father place them but before the gate of his Heart? Does not all human joy, which is in the *whole* man, arise from the fountain of the heart? In the same way, in God, the great joy arises out of the fountain of his Heart.

24. And therefore he has created the holy angels out of himself; they are, as it were, *little gods* <note>original: "little Gods"; meaning divine beings who reflect God's nature on a smaller scale</note>, corresponding to the being and qualities of the whole God. In that power, they should *act out* the praise, and sing and ring forth in the power, increasing the joy that arises from the heart of God.

25. But the splendor and the power of the Son of God (or Heart of God), who is the *Light* or source and fountain of joy, has his most beautiful and joyful origin <note>original: "original"</note> in the center or *midst* of these kingdoms, and shines into and through all the angelic gates.

26. You must understand this *correctly*: when I speak by way of analogy <note>original: "similitude"</note> and compare the Son of God to the sun or to a round globe, it does not mean that he is a limited <note>original: "circumscriptive"</note> fountain that can be *measured*, or whose depth, beginning, or end could be fathomed. I write this way only by way of analogy until the *reader* can come to the true understanding.

27. For the meaning here is not that the Son of God is generated *only* in the center or midst of these angelic gates, and nowhere else outside, beyond, or *beside* these angelic gates.

28. For the powers of the Father are *everywhere*, and it is from and out of these powers that the Son is generated and the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> goes forth. *How* then could he be generated only in the center of these angelic gates?

29. This, therefore, is the only basis <note>original: "ground"</note> and meaning: that the Holy Father, who is ALL, desired to *have* his most joyful and most richly loving qualities <note>In this context, "qualities" refers to the fundamental divine forces or "source-spirits" that constitute God's being.</note> in these angelic gates. From these qualities, the most joyful and most *richly loving* Light, Word, Heart, or fountain of powers is generated. And therefore, he has created his holy angels in this place for his joy, honor, and glory.

# The Eighth Chapter.

### Of the whole Corpus <note>Latin: "body"</note> or Body of an Angelic Kingdom.

## The Great Mystery.

->1.<-

The angelic kingdoms are *entirely* formed according to the Divine Being; they have no other form or condition than the *Divine Being* has in its Trinity.

2. Only this is the difference: their bodies are *creatures* <note>meaning created beings</note> which have a beginning and an end. Furthermore, the kingdom where their *local residence* <note>original: "Locality habitation"</note> or court is located is not their own bodily property or personal possession held by *natural right*, in the way they possess their bodies by *natural right*.

3. Instead, the kingdom belongs to God the Father, who has made it out of his powers, and he may establish it and *arrange* <note>original: "dispose"</note> it in whatever way he pleases. Otherwise, their body is made according to and out of all the *powers* of the Father.

4. And their power generates the light and knowledge *within them*. Just as God generates his Son out of *all his powers*, and as the Holy Spirit goes forth out of all the powers of the Father and the Son, so also in an angel, the spirit goes forth from their heart, from their light, and from *all their powers*.

The Third Quality or the Third Spirit of God, within the Father’s power, is the *bitter quality*. This is a penetrating or driving force through the *sweet* and *astringent* (or *harsh*) qualities; it is *trembling, penetrating*, and *rising upward.*

# IV.

## On the Fourth Circumstance or Type

->59.<-

The fourth quality—or the fourth <term>fountain-spirit</term> <note>original: "fountain-Spirit"; Boehme uses this term to describe the primary forces or "sources" flowing from God that create all reality.</note> in the divine power of God the Father—is **Heat**. This is the true **beginning of life**, and also the true **Spirit of Life**.

60. The astringent (harsh and sour) and the sweet qualities together form the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; an alchemical term used by Boehme to refer to the divine "earth" or the basic substance of the celestial realm.</note>, which belongs to the body and is the substance from which the body is built.

61. For coldness and hardness reside in the astringent quality, which acts as a force of contraction and drying; and within the **sweet** quality reside the water, the light or radiance, and the entire physical substance of the body.

62. The bitter quality provides the **separation** and the shaping of forms, while the **heat** acts as the spirit or the kindling of life. Through this heat, the spirit exists within the body; it surges or moves through the whole body and shines outward from it. This heat also creates the **living motion** within all the qualities of the body.

63. There are two main things to observe in all the **qualities**: if you look at a body, you first see the <term>stock-pith</term> <note>original: "Stock Pith"; meaning the central core, essence, or structural foundation of a thing.</note> or the kernel of all the qualities. This core is framed or **composed** of all the qualities together; for the body contains the astringent (harsh and sour), sweet, bitter, and hot qualities. When these qualities are dried together, they form the body or the "stock" (the substance).

# The Ninth Chapter.

->On the Gracious, Lovely, Blessed, Friendly, and
Merciful Love of God.<-

->The Great Heavenly and Divine 
Mystery.<-

->I.<-

Because I write here about heavenly and divine things, which are completely foreign to the corrupt, fallen <note>original: "perished"</note> nature of man, the reader will undoubtedly wonder at the simplicity <note>original: "simplicity"; here referring to the author’s lack of formal academic training or humble social status.</note> of the author and be offended by it.

2. This is because the condition and inclination of our fallen nature is to gaze only on "high" things, like a proud, wild, reckless, and promiscuous woman who always gazes in her lustful passion after handsome men to commit acts of indecency with them.

3. In this same way, the proud, corrupt, and ruined nature of man stares only at what is glittering and fashionable in this world. It imagines that God has forgotten the afflicted, and that he plagues them because he does not care for them.

4. Corrupt nature imagines that the Holy Spirit regards only high things—the sophisticated arts and sciences of *this world*, deep academic studies, and great learning.

<meta>catchword: 5. But</meta>

5. But whether it be so or not, look back and you will find the true foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>: What was Abel? A shepherd. What were Enoch and Noah? Plain, simple men. What were Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? Herdsmen.

6. *What was Moses*, that dear man of God? A herdsman. *What was David* when the mouth of the Lord called him? A shepherd.

7. *What were the great and minor <note>original: "Small"</note> prophets?* Common <note>original: "Vulgar"</note>, plain, and humble <note>original: "mean"</note> people. *Some of them were only* country people and herdsmen, *considered the underlings or footstools of the world;* men considered them nothing but mere fools.

8. And though they performed miracles and wonders and showed great signs, yet *the world* gazed only on high things, and the *Holy Spirit* <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> was treated like the dust under their feet; for the proud Devil always endeavored to be king in this world.

9. *And how did our King* JESUS CHRIST *come into this world?* Poor and in great trouble and misery, *and he had nowhere to lay his head* (Matthew 8:20).

10. *What were his apostles?* Poor, despised, uneducated <note>original: "illiterate"</note> fishermen. *And who were those who believed their preaching?* The poorer and humbler <note>original: "meaner"</note> sort of people. The high priests and scribes *were the* executioners of Christ, who *cried out, "Crucify him, crucify him!"* (Luke 23:21).

23. First there is the astringent <note>original: "astringent," meaning a contracting, harsh, or binding force</note> quality, *then* the sweet, and next the bitter. 24. For example, when a man takes a stone, or any hard object, and rubs it against wood, these two things are heated. Now, this heat is nothing but darkness, having no light within it; and it is the same way within the divine power.

25. Now, the astringent and bitter qualities *without* the sweet water rub and drive themselves *so hard* against one another that they generate dark heat, and so they are *kindled* within themselves.

All the creatures in heaven and in this world are imaged, fashioned, or framed out of these spirits, and they live in them as in their own *property* <note>original: "propriety"; here meaning one's own essential nature or private domain</note>.

76. And their *life* and *reason* are generated within them in the same manner as the Divine Being is generated, and also by the *same power*.

77. And from that same *Body* of the seven Spirits of God, all things are made and produced: all angels, all devils, the heaven, the earth, the stars, the elements, humans, beasts, birds, and fish.

48. Instead, the Devil and the wrath hang in the "outward birth" <note>the external, physical manifestation of the spiritual world</note> of the **word**, and the wrath helps to form everything in the outermost manifestation of this world—whatever exists in a tangible or graspable form. This is just like how the astringent and bitter qualities rouse themselves after the initial sound to help shape the word, operating or uniting with it.

94. But because the spirit first passes over the astringent and bitter qualities without being noticed, it signifies that the **Gate of God** is everywhere throughout this world. The Holy Spirit rules there, and Heaven stands open everywhere, even in the very center of the Earth. The Devil can nowhere see, understand, or grasp Heaven. He is like a grumbling and snarling **Hell-Hound** who only emerges from behind after the Holy Spirit has built a Church and Temple for Himself. Then, the Devil tries to destroy it in his wrath; he hangs at the back of the word like an enemy who will not tolerate a Temple of God being built in "his" land, because it would lessen or diminish his kingdom.

<summary>Böhme explains that while the material world and the divine realm coexist in one "body," the Devil and God's wrath are confined to the external, tangible manifestation of reality and cannot perceive the spiritual Heaven that exists everywhere. He uses the phonetic structure of speech as a metaphor for how the Holy Spirit precedes and transcends the harsh, "bitter" qualities of the material world.</summary>

# The Twenty-First Chapter.
## Concerning the Third Day.

->1.<-

Although the *Spirit* in the writings of *Moses* has kept the deepest mysteries hidden and concealed within the literal text <note>original: "Letter"; Böhme often distinguishes between the "Letter" (literal meaning) and the "Spirit" (inner mystical meaning) of Scripture</note>, yet everything is described so very regularly that there is no defect at all in its order.

2. For when God, through the Word, had created Heaven and Earth, and had separated the Light from the Darkness and given a place to each of them, then each presently began its birth <note>original: "Geniture"; the process of generating or bringing forth life</note> and its operating or working.

3. On the **First Day**, God drove together [or compacted] the corrupt <term>Salitter</term> <note>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the fundamental divine substance or "salt-niter" of the universe, which can be either holy or "corrupted" by wrath</note> which became so through the kindling of His wrath. I say, God then drove it together or created it through the strong Spirit; for the word **Schuff** <note>original: "Schuff"; the German word *schuf* means "created," but Böhme interprets the sound of the word as a "shoving" or driving together of matter</note> signifies here a "driving together" or "compaction."

4. In this driving together or compaction of the corrupted wrath-Salitter, King *Lucifer* was also—as a powerless prince together with his angels—driven into the "hole" of the wrath-Salitter. He was driven into that place where the outward, half-dead tangibility <note>original: "comprehenſibility"; referring to the physical world that can be perceived and grasped by the senses</note> is generated, which is the place or space between the nature-goddess, the *Moon*, and the dead *Earth*.

5. Now when this was done, the Deep became clear,

5. ...clear, and with the hidden or concealed *Heaven*, the *Light* was separated from the *Darkness*, and the globe of the Earth in the great *wheel* of Nature was rolled or turned *once around*. Accordingly, there passed the time of *one revolution*, or of *one day*, which contains twenty-four hours.

6. During the *Second Day*, the sharp *separation* began; the *incomprehensible chasm* <note>original: "Cliffe"; here meaning a "cleft" or abyss (German: *Kluft*) that separates two distinct realms</note> between the *Wrath* and the *Love* of *Light* was made. Thus King *Lucifer* was firmly and strongly *bolted up* into the House of *Darkness* and was reserved for the final *Judgment*.

7. In this way, the water of *Life* was also separated from the water of *Death*. Yet, they are joined to one another in this temporal world like *Body* and *Soul*, and yet neither of them can fully grasp <note>original: "comprehend"; used here in the sense of one substance containing or penetrating another</note> the other. The *Heaven* which was made out of the midst or center of the *water* is the *divide* <note>original: "Cliffe"</note> between them, so that the tangible or physical water is a *Death*, and the intangible or spiritual water is the *Life*.

8. Thus, the incomprehensible *Spirit*, which *is God*, now rules everywhere in this world and *fills all things*. The tangible world depends upon Him and dwells in the *Darkness*; it can neither see, hear, smell, nor feel the incomprehensible Spirit, but it sees His works and is a *destroyer* of them.

9. And now, when God had bound up the *Devil* in the *Darkness* through the *sealing* of the *Heaven*—which *Heaven* is present everywhere in all places—He began again His wonderful *birth* or *generation* <note>original: "Geniture"; Böhme's term for the ongoing process of divine creation and manifestation</note> in the *seventh* nature-spirit, and everything was generated again just as *it had been from eternity*.

11. This indeed is described very rightly and properly, but the true foundation <note>original: "ground"</note> remains hidden or concealed in the Word, and has *never* been understood by man. For since the Fall, man could never comprehend or understand the inward birth <note>original: "Geniture"; refers to the process of generation or the way things are spiritually produced</note> to perceive what the heavenly birth is like. Instead, his *reason* lay captivated by outward, physical things <note>original: "comprehensibility or palpability"</note> and could not penetrate or press through to Heaven to see the inward birth of God, which is also in the corrupted earth and *everywhere* in all places.

12. You must *not* think here that God has made some *new* thing which *never* existed before. For if that were so, then there would have been another God, which is not possible. For without, or *besides*, this one and only God, nothing exists at all; even the gates of Hell are *not anywhere* outside, beyond, or absent from this one and only God. There is only a *partition* or distinction between the love in the light and the kindled wrath in the darkness, so that the one cannot comprehend the other, and yet they are joined together as *one body*.

13. The *Salitter* <term>Salitter</term> <note>Salitter: A term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the fundamental divine substance or "spiritual saltpeter" that makes up the earth and the heavens.</note>, out of which the earth has come to be, was from eternity; and stood in the seventh quali-

It forms or frames *another* body, which stands half in death and half in life, and stands *hidden* between the wrath of God and His love.

According to this Third Birth, the earth shall be purged and cleansed at the end of this time and shall be set or put again into its *original* place; but the wrath will remain in death.

For the *life* which exists in the *Light* cannot raise itself within the *hard, bitter, and astringent body*; for it is held captive in the *cold fire*, though it is *not* entirely dead.

<note>original: "Morning-Rednesse"; this is the English translation of the book's original German title, *Morgenröte*, which refers to the light of God's grace rising in the soul.</note>

[27. ...the account of Creation was] not *described in writing*, but was kept as an obscure tradition <note>original: "Dark word." 29. And it was the *primary instruction* and *doctrine* of the Patriarchs before and after the Flood that they *guided men to the Creation*, just as the whole book of Job also aims at that.

30. After these Patriarchs came the wise *pagans* <note>original: "Heathens."</note>, who went somewhat deeper into the knowledge of *Nature*. 31. 32. Indeed, they honored, prayed to, or *worshiped* the sun and stars as gods, but they did not know how they were created or came to be, or out of what [they were made]...
