50. Yes, dear man, now boast to yourself that you have hit the mark well! You indeed know God better than others. Behold, you blind man: wherever love rises up in meekness, there the *Heart of God* rises up. For the Heart of God is generated in the meek water of the kindled Light—whether it be in man, or anywhere else outside of man—it is *everywhere* generated in the center, between the outermost and innermost birth <note>original: "geniture"</note>.

51. And whatever you look upon, God is there; but the *comprehensibility* <note>the capacity to be perceived or grasped by the senses and reason</note> exists in this world within the wrath that the Devil has kindled. In the hidden kernel in the midst or center of the wrath, the light or Heart of God is generated, remaining *incomprehensible* <note>unable to be grasped or overtaken</note> to the wrath, and so each of them remains in its own place.

52. Yet for all that, I in *no way* approve of or excuse the *unbelief* of the Jews, Muslims <note>original: "Turks," a standard Early Modern term for Muslims</note>, and heathens, nor their stiff-necked stubbornness, their fierce wrath, or their furious malice and hatred against Christians. No; these things are mere snares of the Devil, by which he allures men to pride, covetousness, envy, and hatred, so that he may kindle in them the hellish fire. Neither can I say that these "four sons of the Devil" <note>referring to the four vices just mentioned: pride, covetousness, envy, and hatred</note> are *not* dominating in Christendom; indeed, they dominate in every man.

### 53. **Here the Spirit opens both doors and gates; if you will not see, then remain blind.**

54. The first difference is one that God has always held and maintained: that all those who *know* what God is and how they should serve Him should be *able*, through their knowledge, to *push* through the wrath <note>In Boehme’s theology, "wrath" is the dark, fire-principle of God that must be overcome by the light of love</note> into God's Love and overcome the Devil. But if they do *not* do so, then they are no better than those who do *not* know it.

55. But if someone who does *not* know the way *pushes* through the wrath into Love, then they are like the person who pushed through *by* their knowledge. But those who persist in the wrath and completely kindle it within themselves are all alike, one and all, whether they are Christians, Jews, Muslims <note>original: "Turks"</note>, or heathens.

->Or what do you suppose it is by which<-
->a human being can serve God?<-

56. But he who has *Love* in his heart, and leads a merciful, meek, and humble life, and *fights* against malice and hatred, and *pushes* through the wrath of God into the Light—he lives with God and is *one spirit* with God.

57. For God requires no other service but that His creature, who exists within *His Body* <note>Boehme often describes the universe as the "body" of God</note>, does not slide back away from *Him*, **but remains holy, just as He is.**

# The Gate of the Holy Trinity.

67. **The entire Birth or Generation** <note>original: "Geniture"; the eternal process of divine creation and becoming.</note> which is the Heaven of all Heavens, as well as this world—which is *within* the Body of the whole—as well as the place of the Earth and of all creatures, and whatever you can think of: **all of that together is God the Father.** He has neither beginning nor end; and wherever and whatever you think upon, even in the smallest circle that can be imagined, there is the *entire* Birth or Generation of God, perfectly, incessantly, and irresistibly.

68. But if the light is extinguished in any creature or in any place, then the austere Birth or Generation <note>original: "austere Geniture"; in Böhme’s theology, this refers to the harsh, rigorous, or wrathful quality of nature that exists when the light is withdrawn.</note> is *there*, which lies hidden within the Light in the innermost kernel. **And this is now the First Part.**

69. **The second part or the second Person is the Light,** which is continually generated from or out of all powers, and enlightens all the powers of the *Father* once again, and has the fountain of all powers. But it is distinguished from the Father as a *distinct Person*, in that it cannot encompass the Birth or Generation of the Father, and yet is the Father’s *Son*, who is always generated from or out of the Father. You have an example of this in all the kindled *fires* in this world; just consider them.

### Chapter XXIV. Of the Incorporating of the Stars.

But on the third day, life broke through death, and the *new* birth began.

43. He did this so that this time might once again be *one* with eternal time, ensuring no "day of death" stands *between* them. He intended that eternal love and the reborn—or regenerated—love from nature's new body might be *one* eternal *love*. There should be *no* difference between eternal love and the newborn love; rather, the newborn love should reach into the very essence <note>original: "Being or Substance"</note> that existed from eternity, and exist within eternity itself.

44. 21. 22. But the true Heaven is everywhere, all around us, *up to this very time* and until the Last Judgment Day. Likewise, the wrath-house of Hell and of Death is also in this world *everywhere*, even to the Last Judgment Day.

# The Kindling of the Heart or Life of this World.

32. # **Of the Whole Body of this Astral World.** Chapter 25.

46. Dear Reader, I understand the *astrologers’* meanings and sayings full well, and I have perused their writings also, and taken notice of how they describe the course of the *Sun* and *stars*. I do not despise this, but hold it to be for the most part good and right.

47. But that I write differently than they do in some things, I do not do out of self-will, conceit, or mere supposition—doubting whether it be so or not. I dare not have any doubt here, nor can any man instruct me in this matter.

48. I have not gained my knowledge through study. Indeed, I have read of the order and *position* of the *seven planets* in the books of astrologers and find them to be very correct; but the Root—how they came to be and from what they proceeded—I cannot learn from any man. For they do not know it, nor was I present when God created them.

49. But because the Doors of the Deep, the Gates of Wrath, and the Chambers of Death are set open in my spirit through the Love of God, the spirit, *therefore*, must necessarily look through them.

50. 80. The reason the light could take *no* sooner hold of it was because of its intense fierceness and sudden flash; it was not captured by the *light* until the light had completely or thoroughly influenced or possessed it.

81. And there it remains now as a "tyrant rager" and stirrer of the whole body of *this* world. For that is its very office <note>purpose or function</note>: that with its *revolution* in the wheel of nature, it moves and stirs everything—which is where all life takes its origin.

# The Twenty-Sixth Chapter

## *Of the Planet Saturn*

-> 1. <-

Saturn—that cold, sharp, austere, and astringent ruler—does not take its beginning or origin from the *Sun*. For it has the chamber of death within its power and is a dryer-up of all powers, from which physicality <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> originates.

2. For just as the *Sun* is the heart of life and the origin of all spirits in the body of this world, so Saturn is the source of all physicality <note>original: "corporeity"</note> and comprehensibility or tangibility. The whole body of this world exists within the power of these two planets. There cannot be *any* creature, any formation <note>original: "imaging"</note>, or any movement <note>original: "mobilitie"</note> without the power of these two in the natural body of this world.

# Chapter XXVI. Of the Planet Mercury.

68. *No!* For the clear Deity stands everywhere hidden in the circle, in the heart of the whole Deep <note>original: "Deepe"; the infinite, divine space underlying all existence</note>. The seven spirits stand in the body of the Deep in anxiety and great longing, and are continually ignited by the planets and stars; from this arises the *mobility* and the birth-process <note>original: "Geniture"; the ongoing process of generation or creation in nature</note> in the whole Deep.

69. But since the heart of the Deity hides itself in the body of this world—in the outermost birth or generation, which is materiality <note>original: "corporeity"; the physical, external state of the universe</note>—*because of this*, materiality is a dark house. Everything exists in great anguish and needs a *Light* to shine in the chamber of darkness, which is the **Sun**. This will continue until the heart of God *moves* itself again within the seven spirits of God in the house of this world and *ignites* the seven spirits.

70. And then the *Sun* and stars will return again to their first place and will pass away in that form or manner. For the heart and light of God shall give light and shine again in the *corporeality*—that is, in the body of this world—and replenish or fill everything.

71. And then the anxiety ceases; for when the anxiety in the governance of the generative process <note>original: "Dominion of the Geniture or Birth regiment"; the natural forces that govern how things are born and grow</note> tastes the *sweetness* of the light of God—so that the heart of God triumphs together in the birth-governance—then all is richly full of joy, and the whole body triumphs.

72. At present, in this time, this *cannot be* in the house of this world because of the fierce, captive devil who keeps house in the outermost birth or generation in the body of this world until the judgment of God.

# Of Man and the Stars.

74. Just as the Deep <note>original: "Deepe"; the vast, hidden spiritual foundation of the universe</note>—or the house of this world—is a dark house where the whole of materiality <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> generates itself, and is therefore very thick, dark, anxious, and half-dead, taking its movement from the planets and stars which ignite the body in the outermost birth-process <note>original: "Geniture"; the ongoing process of creation and manifestation in nature</note>—from which arises the mobility of the elements, as well as the shape and being of every creature—so too the human house of flesh is a *dark valley*. Within it, there is indeed the anguish of the birth of life; it always strives upward, intending to elevate itself into the *Light*, from which *Life* might ignite itself.

113. By this, a *mass*, *seed*, or driving will and desire to propagate another human being immediately arises in the *mass* <note>original: "Masse"; here referring to the physical and spiritual substance or "clay" from which life is formed</note>.

114. In exactly this same way and manner, the first *mass* also came to be. For the Love-Spirit in the heart of God cast a glance into the body of the ignited, <term>wrathful Father</term> <note>In Boehme’s theology, the "Father" represents the raw, fiery power of nature and justice, while the "Son" or "Heart" represents divine love</note> upon the *water* of life. Through this glance, the *love* in the <term>fire-flash</term> <note>the moment of ignition where raw energy becomes light or consciousness</note> arose and sprang up *before* the time of the wrath.

115. In this casting of the glance, one spirit caught the other. The oily *oil* or water in the wrath conceived from the Love-Spirit in the heart of God, and <term>qualified</term> <note>original: "qualified"; merged or interacted with</note>, mixed, or united with it. Then the <term>astringent spirit</term> <note>the contracting or "pulling" force of nature</note> drew the *mass* together. There was clearly a birth, a will, or a desire to produce a whole creature, just as the *seed* is in a *man*.

116. But now, the <term>firmament of heaven</term> <note>the boundary between the physical/fallen world and the divine realm</note>—which is *between* the heart of God and the ignited, hard <term>chamber of death</term> <note>the state of harsh, cold nature separated from God's light</note>—was closed or shut up. Otherwise, the life in the *mass* would have suddenly ignited itself.

117. For the firmament was both *within* the *mass* as well as *outside*, distinct from the *mass*. It is the parting mark, or limit of separation, between the heart of God and the fierce devils.

118. Therefore, the *Word* or heart of God had to breathe into <note>original: "blow up"</note> the moving spirit in the *mass*, which was only done on the sixth day for very certain reasons.

# Chapter XXVI: Of Man and the Stars

119. For if Heaven, as a firmament, had not been enclosed within the *mass* <note>original: "Masse"; the primordial physical and spiritual substance of the human body</note>—between the Heart of God and the corporeal <term>fountain spirits</term> <note>the fundamental spiritual forces or energies that make up all reality in Boehme's cosmology</note> of that *mass*—then the *mass* might have ignited the soul through its own power, just as happened with the holy angels.

120. But it was feared that what happened to that beautiful young son *Lucifer* would happen again; he was composed of the corporeal fountain spirits in the *mass* which were ignited in the <term>wrath-fire</term> <note>the harsh, consuming, or "angry" aspect of divine power and nature, separate from light and love</note>.

121. Therefore, Heaven must be a firmament—a protective boundary—placed before the spark that was conceived from the Heart of God in that first glance. This was done so that even if the body should happen to perish, the holy seed might remain. This seed is the *soul*, which <term>qualifies</term> <note>original: "qualifyeth"; interacts, merges, or operates in harmony with</note>, mixes, or unites with the Heart of God. From this soul, a *new body* might eventually emerge when God once again ignites the depths of this world in the light of His Heart. And this is exactly how it has come to pass with the body.

## *May the Love of God have mercy and take pity on it.*

122. The dear man *Moses* writes 

### *that God made Man out of a Clod of Earth,*

as the learned scholars have translated it. However, *Moses* was not present when this was done.

123. The spirit has kept this hidden until *this very time.*

133. 136. For when the Love-Spirit from the heart of God glanced on the *salitter* of the *mass*, the *salitter* caught hold of it and conceived from it, and was impregnated in the *center* of the soul. The *word* stood in the *mass* as a sound, but the *light* remained in the center of the *mass* in the firmament of heaven, staying hidden in the unctuous oil <note>meaning oily or rich; here referring to the spiritual essence that fuels the divine light</note> of the heart, and did *not* move itself forth out of the firmament of heaven during the birth of the qualifying or fountain spirits.

137. However, since the wrath had clearly already infected the salitter, that same danger was to be feared which befell *Lucifer*.

144. But for all that, I cannot forbear <note>original: "forbeare"; refrain or keep silent</note>. 146. Therefore, I can bring it no further than from the *heart* into the *brain*, before the princely throne of the senses. For if that were done, I would tell it with my mouth and make it known to the world.

This copy <note>original: "ex." (exemplaar)</note> matches exactly with the description from Buddecke II, 98: <note>Werner Buddecke (1902–1991) was a German bibliographer famous for his definitive catalog of the works of the mystic Jacob Böhme.</note>

- [1 recto: blank] <note>original: "blanco"</note>
- 1 verso: "Revelation 1:4" = the biblical passages associated with the engraving
- inserted: engraving
- 2 recto: title
- [2 verso: blank]
= A recto Note [etc.]

Therefore, there are two unsigned leaves plus an engraving before signature A. <note>In historical printing, "signatures" are letters at the bottom of pages used to guide the binder; "unsigned leaves" are pages that lack these marks.</note>
